decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule requires ALL C1-C8 for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. C4 fails (2/5 < 3/5 patterns with positive savings) and C6 fails (r=0.3909 < 0.7, savings do not correlate with value length). The hypothesis that parameterized representation saves tokens for long-value URL patterns as a general claim is falsified under tiktoken cl100k_base. However, the ceiling is stratified: single-slot genuinely long values DO save tokens (UUID 36-char +44.44%, bearer 64-char +56.72%) while multi-slot patterns with short per-slot values penalize even at long total string length (P3 -11.54%, P5 -9.68%). Audit REVISE status accepted: arithmetic verified exactly, but 'long-value' label is misapplied to P3/P5 (per-slot values are 3-5 chars, not long), and mean 15.99% is bimodal and misleading as a standalone statistic. C1-C3 and C7-C8 pass, confirming resolve/bind pipeline works correctly for long values and kernel regression is intact.

claim_updates.reason: Resolve/bind pipeline validated for 5 long-value patterns (7/7 EXECUTABLE with correct params, 7/7 UNKNOWN when missing, _bind correct for 1-3 slots). However, token savings hypothesis for long values is falsified as a general claim: only 2/5 patterns (single-slot UUID and bearer) save tokens; 2/5 multi-slot patterns penalize; 1/5 slug breakeven. The frozen gate fails (C4, C6). Per-slot concrete value length and slot count are the causal factors, not total string length. Claim ceiling bounded to: committed-code synthetic single-slot with prefix metadata for resolve/bind pipeline, token savings demonstrated ONLY for single-slot patterns where per-slot concrete value >> slot name + 3. NOT product-ready. Do not advance to VALIDATED or PRODUCT_CORE.

Token economics hypothesis remains HYPOTHESIS. Short-value penalty (parent -6.4%) and long-value stratified result (single-slot saves, multi-slot penalizes) jointly close the general token-savings argument: parameterized representation does NOT reliably save tokens across URL patterns. However, C-PRODUCT-ECON's broader claim (amortized deduplication savings across tasks offset per-mechanism token penalty) is orthogonal to per-mechanism token count and remains untested. The product lane should pivot to measuring end-to-end amortized cost with model calls, browser, retrieval and verification if the deduplication hypothesis is to be pursued.

product_action: No product promotion. C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS. No code changes to production. The resolve/bind pipeline is validated but the token-savings economic argument is closed for both short and long values as a general claim.
next_question: Should the product lane pivot to measuring end-to-end amortized cost for C-PRODUCT-ECON (mechanism deduplication savings across tasks where fewer unique mechanisms to store/retrieve offset per-mechanism token penalty), or close token-based inheritance viability entirely and pursue alternative product economics (retrieval efficiency, registry size compression)?
